summary: Sporting News examines whether the 1-7 Carolina Panthers will fire head coach Frank Reich after one season, citing ESPN's Adam Schefter's remarks that owner David Tepper is impatient. Poor offensive play and rookie QB Bryce Young's struggles have put Reich on a hot seat, and the Thursday night game against the Bears carries added weight. The article also reviews Reich's career record with the Colts and Panthers.
one_line: With the Panthers at 1-7, Frank Reich's job looks increasingly shaky as impatient owner David Tepper weighs a change after one season.
key_facts: The Panthers are 1-7 in 2023 and at the bottom of the NFC South, despite preseason optimism after moving on from Matt Rhule and adding Bryce Young.
Bryce Young threw three interceptions, including two pick-sixes to Kenny Moore, in a 27-13 loss to the Colts.
Carolina's offense averages the fifth-fewest yards (283.4) and sixth-fewest points (17.5) per game; the offensive line has allowed 74 pressures, 10th-most in the NFL.
Frank Reich already gave up play-calling to offensive coordinator Thomas Brown after early-season struggles.
Adam Schefter said on "The Pat McAfee Show" that "I don't think anybody's got a long rope there" and that David Tepper "is not very patient."
Schefter pointed to Tepper's in-season firing of Matt Rhule, despite rumors he would wait, as an example of his impatience.
The Panthers play the Bears on Thursday Night Football; the Bears hold the No. 1 draft pick Carolina traded away to select Young.
Reich's career regular-season head coaching record is 41-40-1 in 81 games.
With the Colts, Reich went 40-33-1, with three winning seasons in five campaigns; he was fired after Week 9 of 2022 with a 3-5-1 record.
Reich made the postseason in two of his first three Colts seasons and went 1-2 across three playoff games.
Reich has had a different Week 1 starting quarterback in each of his first six seasons as head coach.
Adam Thielen has looked rejuvenated in Carolina, while running back Miles Sanders has been a bust acquisition.
